about: Pinned data for scripts/check-refusal-strings.py (issue #323 class). Edited by hand on purpose; there is no --update mode.

Every string in the PATCHED .vite/build/index*.js (a literal, or a `"a"+x+"b"` concatenation chain read as one text; texts longer than 300 characters are keyed per sentence) that names the platform, the Linux session, the device or Computer Use and reads like a refusal. Our own js/ strings are subtracted by the script; a string a .nim patch writes inline is pinned here with an 'ours:' reason.

id = first 12 hex of sha1(text); text = normalised (template expressions and concatenation operands -> ${}, whitespace collapsed, source escapes kept as written). sites = how many places print it: a second site fails until reviewed.

status: neutralised (our patch makes the guard in front of it pass, or replaces the text, on Linux; 'verify' names the injected shape that makes it true and must match 'count' times in the bundle) | unreachable (no Linux path reaches it while our patches are active) | accepted (true on Linux, or platform-neutral). A reason starting 'needs review' is waiting for a maintainer decision.
A new 'accepted' entry loosens the gate: it needs @patrickjaja in the commit.
